svg.text: The unpublished structures are not neglect, and they are not a size effect either
anyone reading the PDB's unpublished share as a failure of the
whether an unwritten structure is a gap or a deliverable
unpublished share climbs with depositor size
share of this depositor's entries that were never written up
entries this depositor's name appears on (log scale)
a consortium filing under its own name
the horizontal axis is here to rule something out
Across these 40 depositors the correlation between log entry count and unpublished share is rho +0.16 —
nothing. Every consortium sits high whatever its size, and the individuals span 3.3% to 73.3% at every
size. The pile is not prolific depositors failing to write up; it is a specific programme. The
individuals sitting up among the consortia are structural genomics principal investigators, which is an
inference from outside this table — its falsifier is that their depositions should cluster in 2004–2011,
and that is not tested here.
JCSG has the highest rate, 86.4%, and
runs 48.7% and owns 2,760 — twice the pile
RCSB PDB search API, fetched 2026-09-22. Depositor is `audit_author.name`, a multi-valued field: an entry carries many authors, so entries cannot be
summed across depositors and no “top N account for X%” is computable from it — shares within a single depositor are fine, which is why only those are
drawn. Names also split: `Edwards, A.` has 2,698 entries and `Edwards, A.M.` has 2,331, one person in two buckets; one name in sixty splits this way,
which bounds the damage but had to be measured. Only names with 800 or more entries are shown, forty of them. “Unpublished” means the primary citation
reads “To be published”, recorded at deposition and never revisited.
